money.evidence: in an additional total amount of $78,567.12

output.summary: This amendment adds $78,567.12 to the district's agreement with Bay Alarm Company for monitoring services that use a two-way voice feature to reduce false alarms and burglar alarm signals. It raises the cap from $144,000 to $222,567.12 and extends the term from June 30, 2023 to June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Adds $200,000 for Fagen Friedman & Fulfrost legal services, for a $700,000 cap in 2022-23

money.evidence: in an additional amount of $200,000.00

output.summary: This amendment adds $200,000 to the District's hourly-rate agreement with the law firm Fagen Friedman & Fulfrost LLP, for a total cap of $700,000 for the 2022-23 fiscal year. The firm defends the District against Government Code claims and civil lawsuits, including those about facilities and special education, and gives general legal advice when the Legal Department asks. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Adds $400,000 and a year to Lozano Smith's facilities and construction legal services

money.evidence: in the additional not to exceed amount of $400,000.00

output.summary: This amendment adds $400,000 to the district's agreement with the law firm Lozano Smith for as-needed legal help on facilities and construction matters (not including related claims and litigation defense). It raises the cap from $400,000 to $800,000 and extends the term from June 30, 2023 to June 30, 2024. The original agreement was set up as a memorandum of understanding and engagement policy.

output.headline: Adds $550,000 to California Department of Social Services newcomer student grant and extends it to 2026

money.evidence: additional amount of $550,000.00

output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text's dates are garbled (period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024, "to June 30, 2026"), and it ties the added $550,000 to 2022-2023 while describing work in the 2023-2024 fiscal year.
output.summary: This amendment adds $550,000 to a state grant, raising the agreement's cap from $1,835,520 to $2,385,520, and extends it to June 30, 2026. The grant helps the District support students whose formal schooling was interrupted, including newcomer English learners. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Pays up to $50,130.44 for 2023-24 catastrophic accident insurance for students and volunteers

money.evidence: not to exceed a cumulative cost of $50,130.44

output.summary: The board is approving payment of the 2023-24 premium for catastrophic accident insurance, underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company and paid through broker Myers-Stevens & Toohey & Company. Class I (interscholastic athletics) costs $9,513.08 and Class II (student activities) costs $40,617.36, not to exceed $50,130.44 in total. There is no deductible.

output.headline: Pays up to $75,846.87 for 2023-24 student accident and sickness insurance

money.evidence: not to exceed a cumulative cost of $75,846.87

output.summary: The board is approving payment for student accident and sickness insurance underwritten by ACE American Insurance Company, paid through broker Myers-Stevens & Toohey & Company. Coverage runs July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024 and covers enrolled students for injuries at school, at school activities and while traveling to and from school. The cost cannot exceed $75,846.87, with no deductible.

output.headline: Hires Friedman & Bartoumian for workers' compensation defense, up to $300,000 in total

money.evidence: cumulatively not to exceed $300,000 for the term

output.summary: The district is signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU) and engagement policy with the law firm Friedman & Bartoumian to provide legal help on workers' compensation defense as needed. Spending is limited to $100,000 per fiscal year and $300,000 in total for the term. The text does not give specific start and end dates.

output.headline: Approves agreement with North Region SELPA to share Santa Fe portable costs; SELPA adds $500,000

money.evidence: North Region SELPA contributing $500,000

output.summary: The District and the North Region Special Education Local Plan Area (SELPA) will share the cost of installing portables and related facilities at the Santa Fe site, 915 54th Street in Oakland. The space will house the West Oakland Medical Therapy Unit program. North Region SELPA will contribute $500,000, and the District will cover all remaining costs, which the text does not state.

output.headline: Pays $3,875,121 for property and liability coverage and $806,000 for workers' comp coverage, 2023-24

money.evidence: in the amount of $3,875,121.00

output.summary: The board is approving 2023-24 insurance payments to two pooled insurance groups (joint powers authorities). Excess property and liability coverage through Northern California ReLiEF JPA costs $3,875,121.00, and excess workers' compensation coverage through PRISM (written "PRISIM" in the text) costs $806,000. The text does not state a combined total.

output.headline: Ratifies reappointment of a member to the school facilities bond oversight committee through June 2025
output.summary: The Board is ratifying the Board President's reappointment of Sarah Price, for a second term, to the Independent Citizens' School Facilities Bond Oversight Committee for Measures B, J and Y. The new term runs July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2025.
